title: Strongly minimal models classified by dimension

based_on.title: Model Theory
based_on.pages: 31–32 (§8, Proposition 8.5, Corollary 8.6, Theorem 8.7 and Corollary 8.8; Lent 2023 lecture notes)

summary: Extend specified basis bijections to isomorphisms and derive categoricity above the language-size bound.
abstract: A basis in a strongly minimal model records its algebraically independent points; every other point lies in a finite definable set over that basis. A bijection between two bases first preserves all formulas because generic points have a unique type. It then extends across the algebraic points: a finite candidate set in the target realizes all the required transported conditions. Unions of chains allow this process to cover both models while retaining the original basis bijection. Thus models of a complete strongly minimal theory are isomorphic exactly when they have the same dimension. Above the language-size bound, dimension equals model size, giving one model up to isomorphism at every such cardinal. In a countable language this includes every uncountable cardinal.
